page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head and page number at the top. Marginal notes in the left margin: a Scripture reference beside the first paragraph, a note on "necessitas", and a reference beside the Epictetus quotation.

main_text.l: non effet gens humana ignorantiæ &
perfidiæ heu nimis obnoxium: quo for-
tasse spectant illa Christi verba {a}ἐκ τῶ
πνευμάτος ἔστιν[?] Ergo ficut vitandus est me-
dicinæ usus, ubi ad vitæ conservationem
& valetudinem tuendam non videtur
esse quodammodo necessaria: sic & Ju-
ramentum vitandum, ubi conservandæ
humanæ societatis {o}necessitas, veritatis
manifestatio, & fidei confirmatio, non
videntur ipsius usum aliquo modo effla-
gitare. Salutare monitum est illud Epi-
cteti(ut illius Stoici omnia) ὅρκον πάντως, εἰ δὲ μή[?], ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ[?], ἐν τῶν
ἐνόντων[?]. Jusjurandum devita, si possibile est, omnino: si non, saltem quantum
potes. Sancta res est Juramentum: sed
quo sanctior, eo periculosior, si indebite
adhibeatur. Sicut pharmacum, quo ma-
joris est efficaciæ & virtutis, eo magis
corpori nocet, si temere & imperite su-
matur. Juramenti assertorii in Rep. ne-
cessarius usus est: in publicis præsertim
judiciis, ad veritatem eruendam circa
facta particularia; quo pertinent jura-
menta testium, calumniæ, purgationis, &c.
Extra judicium & in rebus privatis usus
ejus rarior est: potest tamen quando-
que esse necessarius; ubi sc. multum in-
tereft,

note.i: In totum jurare, nisi ubi necesse est, gravi viro parum convenit.

page.notes: The Greek lines are partly uncertain and marked [?]; the Epictetus Greek in particular is read with doubt. The Scripture Greek after {a} is also doubtful. The phrase "ad .veritatem" has a stray dot before "veritatem" as printed, which is left in the text as a possible printing error. Large section of the Greek on the first line is read from a small scan.
